end.summary: Ishita identified square numbers from dot arrays: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25.
end.parentNote: Asha practised drawing square-number pictures and using L-shaped additions to explain growth. Ishita correctly explained that a 3×3 square grows to 4×4 by adding 3+4=7 dots, and used pictures to justify the pattern. They mixed up the shared-corner count in later examples; this was not corrected by the end of the lesson. At home, draw 4×4 and 5×5 dot squares and mark the new row and column, counting the shared corner only once.
